prose.hook: Tucked into the Pyrenees between France and Spain, this landlocked microstate sits astride crossroads that have long mattered for crossing the mountains. Its rugged terrain hasn't stopped it from becoming a tourist hub and duty-free trading point between two much larger neighbors.
prose.physicalGeography: Andorra is a landlocked pocket of Southwestern Europe wedged into the Pyrenees mountains on the border between France and Spain. Its landscape is rugged, made up of mountains cut through by narrow valleys.
prose.climate: The climate is temperate, with snowy, cold winters and warm, dry summers. Avalanches are a recognized hazard given the mountainous terrain.
prose.economy: Andorra has a high GDP and low unemployment, and although not an EU member it uses the euro. It functions as a duty-free area between Spain and France and has built its economy around tourism, especially skiing, along with banking, timber, and furniture; its financial sector has moved away from a tax-haven model toward a modern banking system, and it has recently joined SEPA and the IMF. Tourism was hit hard by COVID-19, and the country is now seeking bigger investments in technology. Its exports include paintings, integrated circuits, cars, orthopedic appliances, and garments.
prose.peopleAndCulture: Andorra's population is linguistically mixed: Catalan is the official language, spoken by 44.1%, alongside Castilian (40.3%), Portuguese (13.5%), French (10%), and English (3%). The population is predominantly Christian, mostly Roman Catholic, at 89.5%. By nationality, Spaniards make up the largest group at 34.3%, followed by Andorrans at 32.1%, Portuguese at 10%, and French at 5.6%.
